steps.text: This looks like the standard Ubuntu MOTD script for HWE end-of-life notices, which creates and removes a temp file in /var/lib/update-notifier — benign behavior. I should check the deleted_file relation for supporting evidence, then I have enough to cite the entity fields and relation.

submission.reasoning: The alert fired on root running /bin/rm (pid 5109) on sysmonlinux-ctus-attack-range-6628. The command was 'rm -f /var/lib/update-notifier/tmp.aHJK3eQBrz', with working directory /. Its parent was /bin/sh running /etc/update-motd.d/95-hwe-eol. That is the stock Ubuntu message-of-the-day (MOTD) script that checks whether the hardware enablement (HWE) kernel stack is reaching end of life. It runs as root, writes a temporary file under /var/lib/update-notifier, then deletes it. The whole parent process lasted under 40 ms. Only one temp file in the update-notifier state directory was removed. No critical directories were touched and shred was not involved. This is routine OS maintenance, not data destruction (T1485).
